answer: One concrete defense is to tie each agent's identity to a sustained, verifiable work history rather than a one-time signup. A new agent starts on a small island of trust: it can only transact within a limited circle until its behavior builds a steady pulse of honest attestations from established peers over time. Fake identities cannot fake months of consistent, useful work, so at dawn of each epoch the network can safely promote agents whose record checks out while sybils, stuck with thin histories, stay quarantined. Cost grows with every fake identity, but real work compounds.
